title: When the Tide Wakes
premise: Sable Ravensworth built a career planning other people's perfect days after his own engagement collapsed, keeping love safely in the past tense. When his family's centennial reunion on Harrow Island demands he arrive with a partner, he hires Wren Calloway, a ferry mechanic and former flame of his college years, to play the part for one weekend. But the performance curdles into something real by dessert, and Sable must decide whether to protect the wedding empire that saved him from ruin or risk it all for a man who sees through every polished lie. The story ends at the last ferry of the season, where Sable chooses Wren over the career, boarding as a passenger instead of an escape artist.
about_author: Theo Eastwick is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent a decade staging other people's happily-ever-afters before turning to fiction. They write love stories set against salt air and family obligation, believing the best romances begin where the performances end.

chapters.title: The Contract of Small Lies
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In his Portland office, Sable finalizes a stranger's flawless wedding while dodging his mother's reunion summons. His sister threatens to expose his single status unless he brings someone real. He signs off on another couple's joy feeling nothing, establishing the hollow competence that defines him.

chapters.title: Salt and Second Chances
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A canceled ferry strands Sable on the Harrow Island dock, where he collides with Wren Calloway, the man he loved and abandoned twelve years ago, now repairing engines with grease-stained hands. Their banter crackles with unfinished history. Sable leaves without explaining why he vanished.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finds Sable waiting at the boathouse with an absurd proposal: be my fake boyfriend for the reunion weekend, paid handsomely. Wren agrees, but for his own reasons—he wants closure, or maybe revenge. He sets one rule: no lying about the past.

chapters.title: Arrival at Ravensworth House
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The reunion begins: forty relatives, one decaying ancestral house, and Sable performing devotion with Wren's hand in his. His mother scrutinizes; his ex-fiancé's brother smirks. Wren plays the role too well, remembering details Sable never told him.

chapters.title: What the Family Keeps
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren navigates dinner-table politics and learns how the Ravensworths erased Sable's past—no photos of college, no mention of Wren himself. He realizes Sable didn't just leave him; he was amputated. Anger softens into something protective.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal Dinner Nobody Planned
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A cousin hijacks the schedule, forcing Sable to improvise an event overnight—his professional genius on full display. Wren becomes his indispensable co-conspirator, and working together feels dangerously like their old rhythm. By midnight they're laughing in the kitchen like nothing broke.

chapters.title: Low Tide Confessions
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Walking the exposed flats at dawn, Wren demands the truth about why Sable disappeared after graduation. Sable admits his father threatened to disinherit him over Wren, and he chose survival. Wren hears it but doesn't forgive—not yet.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. At the reunion's formal dinner, a toast goes wrong and Sable panics; Wren covers for him with a story so tender the whole table believes it—and so does Sable, briefly. Under the table, their hands find each other. The fake date stops being fake.

chapters.title: The Boathouse
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They give in to twelve years of gravity in the boathouse loft. Afterward, Wren asks what happens Monday. Sable gives a corporate non-answer, and Wren sees the wall going back up. Tenderness curdles into dread.

chapters.title: Mother Knows the Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. His mother confronts him privately: she knows Wren is the boy from before, and she offers a deal—end it quietly and inherit control of the company, or keep him and stay regional manager forever. Power dangled like bait. Sable doesn't answer.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A storm cancels ferries for two days, trapping everyone together. Wren overhears Sable on the phone negotiating a merger that would relocate him to New York indefinitely. He says nothing, but starts packing his emotional bags.

chapters.title: Candles and Confessions
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Power out, the family gathers by candlelight and old grievances surface—including Sable's father's cruelty, witnessed by Wren. For once Sable defends himself aloud, and Wren watches him stand up for the first time. Hope flickers again.

chapters.title: The Price List
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren lays it out plainly: he won't be a secret, a phase, or a stepping stone. Sable promises nothing and offers everything, which convinces Wren of nothing. They sleep apart, the width of the house between them.

chapters.title: A Wedding on the Lawn
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Impromptu, two cousins marry on the storm-cleared lawn, and Sable plans it in four hours—a small miracle. Watching vows he no longer believes in, he catches himself imagining his own, with Wren across the grass. Belief returns uninvited.

chapters.title: The Merger Moves
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The merger closes early; New York starts Monday. His mother presents it as fait accompli, reward for good behavior. Sable realizes the empire he built was always her leash. He asks for one day to decide.

chapters.title: What Wren Built Instead
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Sable visits the ferry yard and sees Wren's life: a restored boat, a crew who depend on him, roots grown deep exactly where Sable fled. Wren isn't asking him to stay; he's asking him to choose honestly. Sable can't yet.

chapters.title: The Unraveling
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Cornered at the farewell brunch, Sable lies to his mother about accepting New York while his eyes find Wren across the room. Wren reads the lie instantly. The weekend ends with both men pretending, badly, that it meant nothing.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The final ferry loads at dawn. Wren works the dock, refusing to watch Sable leave—but he watches anyway. The boat pulls out without Sable aboard. Wren's heart does something complicated between relief and terror.

chapters.title: Resignation Letter, Written in Salt
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. On the mainland, Sable walks into his mother's office and resigns—walking away from the inheritance, the title, the gilded cage. She calls it ingratitude; he calls it the first honest thing he's done in twelve years. He drives back to the coast.

chapters.title: The Offer He Can Make Now
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable finds Wren mid-repair and makes no grand gesture—just the truth: he chose wrong once, chose survival twice, and wants, finally, to choose a person. No contract, no payment, no exit strategy. Wren makes him wait a full day.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returns
chapters.summary: Both POVs interwoven. Wren arrives at Sable's rented cottage at dusk with two tickets on next season's first ferry—not an escape, a beginning. They negotiate a real relationship with all the terms on the table. The kiss lands without performance.

chapters.title: Epilogue: First Ferry Out
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, months later. Spring: Sable plans weddings again, but only ones he believes in, from a small office above the ferry yard. At the season's first crossing, they stand at the rail together as Harrow Island rises from the fog. Belonging, at last, needs no audience.
